title: Developing Nemotron 3.5 Lightning NVFP4 with QAD Using NVIDIA Model Optimizer | NVIDIA Technical Blog
gist: NVIDIA details a quantization-aware distillation (QAD) pipeline in its Model Optimizer that compresses the Nemotron 3.5 Lightning model to a 22 GB NVFP4 checkpoint (from 66 GB) with up to 4x higher throughput while holding accuracy near the BF16 baseline. QAD consistently beats post-training quantization alone, recovering accuracy lost to aggressive 4-bit quantization and unlocking agentic/coding benchmark gains.

insights.claim: NVIDIA's Nemotron 3.5 Lightning NVFP4 checkpoint compresses the model from 66 GB full precision to 22 GB by quantizing many weights to 4 bits, while unlocking up to 4x faster throughput and preserving accuracy.
insights.speaker: Seonghee Lee
insights.so_what: 4-bit quantization roughly triples deployable capacity per GPU, lowering inference cost and reinforcing NVIDIA's full-stack inference advantage.
insights.quote: The new Nemotron 3.5 Lightning NVFP4 checkpoint, for example, preserves accuracy while unlocking up to 4x faster throughput. It’s compressed down to 22 GB from the 66 GB full precision checkpoint by quantizing many of its weights to 4 bits.

insights.claim: Both the aggressive PTQ and QAD Nemotron checkpoints share an identical 21.19 GB footprint versus 65.85 GB for the BF16 baseline, so accuracy differences come from the training method rather than extra memory.
insights.speaker: Seonghee Lee
insights.so_what: Isolating method from memory shows QAD delivers free accuracy at the same deployment cost, a clean argument for adopting the tooling.

insights.claim: QAD is a two-stage process: post-training quantization produces a low-precision student from the full-precision teacher, then the student is distilled against the frozen BF16 teacher using KL divergence loss on logits with simulated quantization in every forward pass.
insights.speaker: Seonghee Lee
insights.so_what: A reproducible recipe for teams to squeeze more compression out of open models without retraining from scratch.
insights.quote: QAD uses the original full-precision model (teacher) to teach the quantized model (student).

insights.claim: Because QAD recovers accuracy afterward, teams can quantize more aggressively at the PTQ stage than a PTQ-only recipe would allow, such as taking Mamba linear layers to W4A16 instead of the safer FP8.
insights.speaker: Seonghee Lee
insights.so_what: QAD shifts the feasible precision frontier, letting memory and throughput budgets that would force conservative precision become reachable.
insights.quote: It’s advantageous to quantize more aggressively at the PTQ stage than if PTQ were the final step, because QAD recovers accuracy afterward.

insights.claim: The scale strategy during QAD follows directly from the PTQ recipe: max-calibrated checkpoints lead to dynamic scale QAD that recomputes scales each step, while MSE-based checkpoints lead to frozen scale QAD that locks the calibrated scales and updates only weights.
insights.speaker: Seonghee Lee
insights.so_what: Codifies a decision rule so practitioners choose the training scale handling deterministically from calibration choices.

insights.claim: On aggressively quantized Checkpoint A, PTQ alone reached 96.33% median accuracy recovery while 200 iterations of QAD brought it to 99.72%, improving 10 of 11 benchmarks and returning AIME 2025 to within 0.57 points of BF16.
insights.speaker: Seonghee Lee
insights.so_what: Quantifies how much accuracy distillation reclaims, the core evidence that aggressive quantization is safe with QAD.
insights.quote: Post-training quantization alone landed at 96.33% median accuracy recovery... Two hundred iterations of QAD from that same checkpoint brought recovery to 99.72%

insights.claim: On intermediate RL Checkpoint B, QAD lifted median score recovery from PTQ's 95.84% to 98.53% at an identical 21.19 GB, with the AA v4.1 Index rising 3.45 points from 20.03 to 23.48 against a 24.81 BF16 baseline.
insights.speaker: Seonghee Lee
insights.so_what: Confirms the recovery pattern replicates across checkpoint types, strengthening the generality claim.

insights.claim: For the conservatively quantized final NVFP4 checkpoint, PTQ already sits near BF16 (99.24% vs QAD's 98.97% median recovery), so QAD's benefit shows up on agentic and coding benchmarks, beating PTQ by 3.79 points on Terminal-Bench v2.1 and 1.07 on SWE-Bench Multilingual.
insights.speaker: Seonghee Lee
insights.so_what: Even where median accuracy is saturated, QAD improves the agentic capabilities that matter most for coding-agent deployments.
insights.quote: QAD beats PTQ by 3.79 points on Terminal-Bench v2.1, 1.07 on SWE-Bench Multilingual, 0.65 on HLE

insights.claim: QAD outperforms PTQ because PTQ fixes weights to a low-precision grid and accepts whatever error results, while QAD lets the model continue training against that error and adapt to it, so most degradation is recovered rather than absorbed.
insights.speaker: Seonghee Lee
insights.so_what: Explains the mechanism, framing QAD as the durable technique for pushing precision floors on future models.
insights.quote: PTQ fixes the weights to a low-precision grid and accepts whatever error that produces, while QAD allows the model to continue training against that error and adapt to it

insights.claim: The full QAD recipe ships in NVIDIA Model Optimizer as a single end-to-end launcher (megatron_lm_qad.yaml) that works for both Nemotron 3 Nano and Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, with the final NVFP4 checkpoint published on Hugging Face.
insights.speaker: Seonghee Lee
insights.so_what: Packaging state-of-the-art optimization as a turnkey NVIDIA workflow deepens developer dependence on the CUDA/Model Optimizer stack.
insights.quote: The full QAD recipe ships in NVIDIA Model Optimizer as a single launcher megatron_lm_qad.yaml that runs the whole pipeline end-to-end.
insights.locator: How to run the QAD recipe with Model Optimizer

insights.claim: QAD training runs on NVIDIA hardware at scale, with PTQ calibration on a single NVIDIA DGX B300 and distillation distilled at a constant 5e-6 learning rate across two nodes of 8 GPUs (TP=2, EP=4).
insights.speaker: Seonghee Lee
insights.so_what: The recipe is validated on and tuned for NVIDIA's own DGX systems, tying reproducibility to NVIDIA infrastructure.

insights.claim: The same QAD steps also run through Megatron-Bridge, a PyTorch-native NeMo Framework library that provides bidirectional checkpoint conversion between Hugging Face and Megatron Core.
insights.speaker: Seonghee Lee
insights.so_what: Bridging Hugging Face and Megatron formats lowers switching friction into NVIDIA's training stack for open-model teams.
insights.locator: How to run the QAD recipe with Megatron-Bridge
